context: Intelligence enablement for Cyber Threat Intelligence Platform (CTIP) to augment threat intelligence processing using local LLM for extracting relevant information from unstructured data collected by Cyber Intelligence Centre, serving as single source of threat intelligence for the Bank with compliance requirements for India and Singapore.

userStories.title: AI-Augmented Threat Intelligence Processing
userStories.iWantTo: process unstructured threat intelligence data using local LLM augmentation
userStories.soThat: I can extract relevant threat information at higher scale and consistency than manual processing

acceptanceCriteria.given: unstructured threat intelligence data is available in CTIP
acceptanceCriteria.when: the LLM processing engine is triggered
acceptanceCriteria.then: relevant threat information is extracted and structured with 95% accuracy

acceptanceCriteria.given: multiple data sources are feeding threat intelligence
acceptanceCriteria.then: all sources are processed within defined SLA timeframes

acceptanceCriteria.given: processed threat intelligence is available
acceptanceCriteria.then: data is presented in standardized threat intelligence format

userStories.title: Local LLM Integration and Management
userStories.iWantTo: deploy and manage local LLM instances for threat intelligence processing
userStories.soThat: sensitive threat data remains within bank infrastructure while leveraging AI capabilities

acceptanceCriteria.given: local LLM infrastructure is deployed
acceptanceCriteria.then: all data processing occurs within bank's secure environment

acceptanceCriteria.given: LLM models require updates
acceptanceCriteria.then: models are updated without compromising ongoing operations

acceptanceCriteria.given: processing load varies throughout the day
acceptanceCriteria.then: LLM instances scale automatically to meet demand

userStories.title: Unstructured Data Extraction and Classification
userStories.iWantTo: automatically extract and classify threat indicators from unstructured documents, reports, and feeds
userStories.soThat: I can identify relevant threats more efficiently and reduce manual analysis time

acceptanceCriteria.given: unstructured threat documents are uploaded to CTIP
acceptanceCriteria.then: IOCs, TTPs, and threat indicators are automatically identified and classified

acceptanceCriteria.given: threat feeds contain mixed structured and unstructured data
acceptanceCriteria.then: content is categorized by threat type, severity, and relevance score

acceptanceCriteria.given: extracted threat indicators are available
acceptanceCriteria.then: false positive rate is maintained below 10%

userStories.title: Data Privacy and Governance Compliance
userStories.iWantTo: ensure all threat intelligence processing complies with data privacy regulations and governance requirements
userStories.soThat: the bank maintains regulatory compliance across India and Singapore jurisdictions

acceptanceCriteria.given: threat intelligence data is processed
acceptanceCriteria.then: all processing activities are logged and traceable for regulatory review

acceptanceCriteria.given: personal or sensitive data is detected in threat intelligence
acceptanceCriteria.then: such data is anonymized or excluded from processing per regulatory requirements

acceptanceCriteria.given: data retention policies are in effect
acceptanceCriteria.then: threat intelligence data is securely archived or disposed per governance requirements

userStories.title: Centralized Threat Intelligence Repository
userStories.iWantTo: access a single source of processed and enriched threat intelligence
userStories.soThat: I can make informed security decisions based on comprehensive and up-to-date threat information

acceptanceCriteria.given: multiple threat intelligence sources are processed
acceptanceCriteria.then: consolidated and deduplicated threat intelligence is returned within 2 seconds

acceptanceCriteria.given: threat intelligence is continuously updated
acceptanceCriteria.then: repository is updated in near real-time with freshness indicators

acceptanceCriteria.given: analyst searches for specific threat indicators
acceptanceCriteria.then: relevant results are ranked by relevance, recency, and confidence score

userStories.title: Multi-Jurisdiction Compliance Management
userStories.iWantTo: manage compliance requirements across India and Singapore jurisdictions
userStories.soThat: threat intelligence operations comply with local data protection and privacy laws

acceptanceCriteria.given: threat intelligence contains cross-border data
acceptanceCriteria.then: data handling complies with both Indian and Singaporean data protection requirements

acceptanceCriteria.given: regulatory requirements change in either jurisdiction
acceptanceCriteria.then: system adapts to new requirements within 30 days of regulatory change

acceptanceCriteria.given: compliance audit is requested
acceptanceCriteria.then: complete data lineage and processing history is available for both jurisdictions

userStories.title: Web-Based Intelligence Dashboard
userStories.iWantTo: monitor and visualize threat intelligence processing through a web-based dashboard
userStories.soThat: I can oversee operations, track performance metrics, and identify processing bottlenecks

acceptanceCriteria.given: dashboard is accessed via web browser
acceptanceCriteria.then: real-time processing metrics and threat summaries are displayed within 3 seconds

acceptanceCriteria.given: threat intelligence processing is ongoing
acceptanceCriteria.then: current processing queue, completion rates, and error statistics are visible

acceptanceCriteria.given: historical trend analysis is requested
acceptanceCriteria.when: manager selects time range for analysis
acceptanceCriteria.then: threat volume trends and processing efficiency metrics are visualized

errorAndEdgeCases: LLM model becomes unavailable or experiences degraded performance during high-priority threat processing
Unstructured data contains formats or languages not supported by the extraction engine
Network connectivity issues between CTIP and threat intelligence data sources
Processing queue becomes backlogged during high-volume threat intelligence periods
False positive rates exceed acceptable thresholds due to model drift or data quality issues
Compliance requirements change rapidly requiring immediate system adaptation
Cross-jurisdictional data handling conflicts between Indian and Singaporean regulations
Concurrent user access limits are exceeded during critical threat response scenarios
Data corruption occurs during processing or storage operations
System performance degrades when processing large volumes of multimedia threat content
assumptions: Local LLM infrastructure has sufficient computational resources for anticipated threat intelligence volumes
Threat intelligence sources provide standardized or parseable data formats
Network connectivity between CTIP and external threat feeds is reliable and secure
Bank's existing security infrastructure can accommodate new LLM processing components
Regulatory requirements for India and Singapore remain stable during initial implementation
Cyber Intelligence Centre has trained personnel to operate and maintain the enhanced system
Integration with existing CTIP infrastructure is technically feasible without major architectural changes
Performance requirements can be met with current hardware and software capabilities
Data quality from upstream threat intelligence sources meets minimum processing standards
openQuestions: What specific LLM models and versions will be deployed for different types of threat intelligence processing?
How will the system handle classification and processing of multimedia threat content (images, videos)?
What are the exact data retention and deletion requirements for each jurisdiction?
How will system performance be monitored and what are the specific SLA requirements?
What backup and disaster recovery procedures are required for the threat intelligence processing system?
How will the system integrate with existing SIEM and security orchestration tools?
What training and change management processes are needed for analyst adoption?
How will threat intelligence confidence scores and source reliability be calculated and maintained?

traceability.notes: Core AI-augmented processing functionality with performance and accuracy requirements
Local LLM deployment and management with security and scalability constraints
Unstructured data extraction with classification accuracy and false positive controls
Data privacy and governance compliance with audit trail and retention management
Centralized repository functionality with performance and search capabilities
Multi-jurisdiction compliance management with adaptability and audit support
Web dashboard for monitoring and visualization with performance requirements

tasks: Develop accuracy measurement and validation framework
Implement model deployment and versioning system
Create monitoring and alerting for LLM services
Develop document parsing and extraction engine
Create false positive detection and reduction mechanisms
Integrate with existing threat intelligence formats
Implement audit logging and traceability system
Develop data anonymization and privacy controls
Implement high-performance search and query engine
Build confidence scoring and ranking algorithms
Build audit trail generation for multiple jurisdictions
Implement real-time metrics collection and display
Integrate dashboard with backend processing systems

definitionOfDone: All acceptance criteria are met and verified through testing
Code review completed and approved by senior developer
Security assessment passed with no critical or high-severity findings
Compliance requirements validated for both India and Singapore jurisdictions
Performance benchmarks met under expected load conditions
Documentation updated including user guides and operational procedures
Integration testing completed with existing CTIP infrastructure
Deployment scripts and configuration management updated
sprintPlanning: Sprint 1-2: Infrastructure setup and LLM deployment (US-2)
Sprint 3-4: Core AI processing engine development (US-1)
Sprint 5-6: Data extraction and classification features (US-3)
Sprint 7-8: Compliance framework and privacy controls (US-4, US-6)
Sprint 9-10: Centralized repository and search capabilities (US-5)
Sprint 11-12: Web dashboard and monitoring features (US-7)
Sprint 13-14: Integration testing and performance optimization
Sprint 15-16: User acceptance testing and production deployment preparation
